summary: Polygon reports that Diablo 4's Season of Blood (season 2), arriving Oct. 17, is defined less by its vampire powers than by sweeping quality-of-life changes. Blizzard's Joe Shely and Joe Piepiora explained faster leveling, five new endgame bosses with targeted Unique drops, simpler Nightmare Dungeons, better mounts, permanent Renown progress, and gems and Stash improvements. The team says it could finally react to player feedback this season.
one_line: Diablo 4's Season of Blood leads with quality-of-life upgrades: faster leveling, new endgame bosses, simpler dungeons, better mounts, permanent Renown and Stash improvements.
key_facts: Diablo 4's Season of Blood (season 2) launches on Oct. 17, a few weeks before BlizzCon 2023, where fans expect the first expansion to be announced.
Blizzard claims players will reach the level cap of 100 about 40% faster than in Season of the Malignant, which already increased experience gains versus launch.
Monsters will now match their levels between 55 and 75.
Five new endgame bosses arrive: Grigoire The Galvanic Saint, the Echo of Varshan, The Beast in the Ice, the Dark Master, and the Echo of Duriel.
Unlocking boss encounters requires tasks such as completing Nightmare Dungeons above level 30 or Grim Favors, and each boss has its own pool of Unique items.
The Echo of Duriel (level 100) is the hardest new boss and the only way to farm Uber Uniques; players must kill the four other bosses each time they want to face him.
Players will be able to trade with one another for the items needed to summon Duriel and the other bosses.
Nightmare Sigils now teleport players directly into the dungeon instead of to the door, and several Nightmare Dungeon affixes were reworked to be less obnoxious.
Horses are faster, their dashes break through barricades in roads, and they should get stuck on objects less easily.
Players who fully unlock the Renown track on one character never have to redo it, and no login to that character is needed to propagate the data account-wide.
Gems no longer take up bag space because they are now crafting materials.
Stashes now appear in more locations, including all minor towns with a Waypoint, and can be searched for specific items and affixes.
Shely and Piepiora said season 2 is the first season where the team could really listen to feedback, since Season of the Malignant launched just over a month after Diablo 4's release.
